The percentage of public schools in the United States requiring uniforms has varied across different reporting years, reflecting the conflict due to outdated information across sources. According to the most recent and authoritative data from the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES), 18.8 percent of public schools required students to wear uniforms during the 2019–20 school year [d1][d3]. An earlier NCES figure cited for the 2017–18 school year put the number at 20 percent [d6], while data for 2015–16 showed nearly 22 percent [d2] — a higher figure that has since been superseded by more recent reporting. As of January 2023, one source approximates the figure at roughly one in five (approximately 20%) public schools [d5], broadly consistent with the NCES trend. By contrast, much older data from a 2000 NAESP survey also found 21% of public schools had a uniform policy [d4], and a peer-reviewed study noted that 21% of public school students attended schools with a uniform policy around 2011–12 [d7]. The most credible and up-to-date answer, based on NCES data, is that approximately 18.8 percent of U.S. public schools required uniforms as of the 2019–20 school year [d1][d3].
